## Objective

Take a research project whose code was **never written to be a reproducibility package**…

…and produce a **complete** reproducibility package that **passes first run and completeness check**.

. . .

> The skill embeds the *exact checks the reproducibility team applies as reviewers.*
> Passing its audit means passing completeness check, and skipping the round-trips where most calendar time is lost.

::: {.notes}
Lead with the pain point: most verification failures aren't about bad code, they're about things the author forgot to check. The skill makes forgetting impossible.
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

# Part 1 · Background {background-color="#002A4F"}

## Are we ready?

Before we begin make sure we have everything we need: 

- **Visual Studio Code** installed (available in the Software Center — note: *VS Code*, not Visual Studio)
- One of the two, signed in within VS Code:
  - **GitHub Copilot** (Copilot Chat extension, with a Claude model available), or
  - the **Claude Code extension**, linked to a personal Claude account
- Demo project, available [here](https://github.com/dime-worldbank/ai-research-training/raw/refs/heads/main/sessions/ai-skills-reproducibility/materials/demo-project.zip)
- Our AI skill, available in [our repo](https://github.com/worldbank/wb-reproducible-research-repository/tree/main/ai-skills/reproducibility-skill); [direct download](https://github.com/worldbank/wb-reproducible-research-repository/releases/download/skill-v2026.07.08/reproducibility-skill.zip)  


## What is an AI skill?

A **skill** is a folder of instructions, scripts, and resources that an AI agent reads to improve performance on specialized tasks. When you ask it to complete a task, the agent reviews the available skills, loads the relevant ones, and applies their instructions.

Our skill...

```
.agents/skills/reproducibility-skill/
├── SKILL.md              # A 4-phase workflow 
├── references/
│   ├── checklist.md      # official WB package requirements
│   ├── flags.md          # 14 common failure flags with detection patterns
│   └── datasets.md       # WDI, PWT, OECD, ILO — licenses and citation formats
└── assets/
    ├── README_template.md # Our reproducibility README template
    ├── README_example.md  # Example of a great README
    └── main.do / main.R / main.py # Example of main files for projects
```

. . .

The agent loads it **only when triggered**, and reads the actual reference files, not its memory of them.

::: {.notes}
Key point: the skill ships the standard as readable files. The agent can be wrong about what it remembers; it can't be wrong about what's in front of it.
:::

## Why a skill, and not just a prompt?

The reproducibility standard is too long to paste into a chat reliably: full checklist + **14 failure flags** based on the reproducibility team experience + assets and references.

. . .

| Without the skill | With the skill |
|---|---|
| You remember to check a few things | The agent checks **every item**, every time |
| Standard lives in someone's head | Standard lives in files the agent reads |
| Each conversation starts from scratch | Guardrails are built into the workflow |
| Standard changes → tell everyone again | Update one file → everyone's next run uses it |

## Skills architecture

Every skill has the same three-part shape — ours included:

```
reproducibility-skill/
├── SKILL.md              ← always loaded once the skill triggers
├── references/           ← opened on demand, only when a phase needs them
│   ├── checklist.md          the official package requirements
│   ├── flags.md               F1–F14 detection patterns
│   └── datasets.md           WDI/PWT/OECD/ILO citation rules
└── assets/                ← used directly as deliverables, not "read"
    ├── README_template.md
    ├── README_example.md
    └── main.do / main.R / main.py
```

. . .

- **`SKILL.md`** — the dispatcher: short, always read, points to the rest
- **`references/`** — consulted mid-task (e.g. `flags.md` during the audit) — extends what the agent knows
- **`assets/`** — copied or filled in (e.g. `README_template.md` becomes the actual README) — extends what the agent produces

::: {.notes}
One diagram, three bullets — keep it tight. SKILL.md dispatches; references get consulted; assets get produced or copied. That's the whole architecture, and it's why the skill can carry far more standard than would ever fit in a prompt.
:::

# Part 2 · The skill {background-color="#002A4F"}

## Four phases, with stop points

| Phase | What happens | Writes files? |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · Audit** | Checks everything against checklist + flags F1–F14; classifies every data file | Read-only |
| **2 · Outline** | Proposes target structure, gap table — the build plan | Proposes only |
| **3 · Build** | Drafts README, DAS, main script; applies approved fixes | After your approval |
| **4 · Run check** | Sets outputs aside, reruns from scratch, verifies every exhibit regenerates | After your approval (you might need to run licensed code) |

::: {.notes}
Emphasize: the agent stops between every phase and waits for approval. It will not write a single file until you've seen and approved the outline. This is the author's control point.
:::

## Phase 1 · Audit — two passes

The agent inventories the project and runs two passes in parallel:

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Checklist pass**

Every required component → **present / partial / missing**, with filename or line as evidence

*(Presence means verified against content, not just that a file exists)*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Flag pass**

Flags F1–F14 → **PASS / FLAG / N/A**, with file and line number

Detection runs actual patterns — hardcoded paths, seeds, install commands, write operations
:::

::::

. . .

**+ Data ↔ README cross-check:** which files does the code *produce* vs. which are *external inputs*? Every external input needs a DAS entry.

## The 14 failure flags (F1–F14) 

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Paths & structure**

- F1 · Hardcoded user-specific paths
- F2 · No single entry point
- F3 · Scattered `cd` / `setwd` in analysis scripts
- F12 · Outputs overwrite inputs

**Randomness & versions**

- F4 · Randomness without a seed
- F5 · User packages not installed by code
- F6 · Software versions not pinned
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Documentation**

- F7 · Manuscript–code version mismatch
- F8 · Input data missing from DAS
- F9 · Outputs not produced by code
- F10 · Missing README / List of Exhibits
- F11 · Extraneous files

**Special cases**

- F13 · Restricted data included by mistake
- F14 · Large-compute pathway not documented
:::

::::

## Phase 1 · Audit: what the agent checks

Goal: report the current state of the project against the standard. **Change nothing.**

. . .

- **Inventory** — every data file, script, output, README, manuscript
- **Checklist pass** — each item recorded as present / partial / missing, with file or line as evidence
- **Flag pass** — F1–F14 run via detection patterns (grep, not eyeballing): hardcoded paths, missing seeds, install commands…
- **README ↔ code** — every script, global, and version claim in the README verified against what the code actually does
- **Data ↔ DAS** — every external input classified, matched to a documented source; unknown provenance = blocking question
- **Exhibit coverage** — every table and figure maps to a script and an output that really gets written

. . .

**And then it stops.** Audit reports the facts, no fixes, no edits. Proposing changes is Phase 2.

## Phases 2–3 · Outline → Build {.smaller}

**Outline** *(nothing written to the project yet)*

- Maps every file into the standard three-folder tree: `data/ · code/ · output/`
- Entry-point rule: replicator changes a path in **exactly one place per language**, at the top of a main script
- Gap table: one row per checklist gap and per flag, with a concrete action to close each
- **Stops again**: you approve, edit, or reject rows before anything is built

. . .

**Build** *(only after approval)*

- README from the standard template: Overview, Data Availability Statement, Instructions, List of Exhibits, Requirements
- Main script(s): version statement, single path global, package installs, seeds, run order
- Re-runs the full Phase 1 audit as a final check

## Phase 4 · Run check

A package that audits clean but has never run from scratch **is not done**.

. . .

1. Build expected-output list from the List of Exhibits
2. Set existing outputs aside — **never deleted without your approval**
3. Rerun from a fresh start, changing only the designated path line
4. Verify every exhibit **regenerates**: fresh timestamp, non-empty, matches previous outputs
5. Record run times → into the README
6. Cleans the project and produces a final reproducibility package. 
7. Reminds author to use this version of exhibits for the manuscript (version control)


Where the agent can’t execute (e.g., Stata): you get the **exact clean-run protocol** as a checklist, designed to catch paths pointing at the old project location.

## Let's set it up {.smaller}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
We'll set up the skill together — I'll walk you through it.
:::

1. **Download & unzip** the demo project, then open it in VS Code
   *File → Open Folder* — select the **folder**, not a file

2. **Add the skill:** create the folder structure and drop the skill in, from vs code terminal, or right-click new folder. 

```{.bash}
mkdir -p .agents/skills
```

Then copy the `reproducibility-skill/` folder into `.agents/skills/` so you have:

```{.plaintext}
demo-project/
├── .agents/
│   └── skills/
│       └── reproducibility-skill/
│           └── SKILL.md
├── data/
├── code/
└── ...
```

3. **Open the Claude Code / Copilot chat panel** and type:

> *"Prepare a reproducibility package for this project."*

The agent reads the skill, detects the match, and starts **Phase 1**.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
We'll use **git** to see what's changing, good practice with AI agents. 
:::

::: {.notes}
Walk people through the VS Code steps before switching windows. Most common issue: opening a file rather than a folder — call this out explicitly and pause to check everyone has the folder open, not a file.

Then walk them through creating `.agents/skills` and dropping the skill folder in — do it live so everyone lands in the same place. If `.agents` doesn't show in the explorer, dot-folders are sometimes hidden; `ls -a` confirms it's there.

On the git tip: reinforce *why* — AI agents can touch a lot of files at once, and `git status` / the diff view is how you stay in control of what you're accepting.
:::

## For your own projects 

Same setup, on your own, a one-time step per project:

1. **Download the skill** from the repo:
   [github.com/worldbank/wb-reproducible-research-repository](https://github.com/worldbank/wb-reproducible-research-repository/tree/main/ai-skills/reproducibility-skill)
   *(or the packaged `.zip` from the [releases page](https://github.com/worldbank/wb-reproducible-research-repository/releases/download/skill-v2026.07.08/reproducibility-skill.zip))*

2. **Create the folder structure** at your project root — from the VS Code terminal:

```{.bash}
mkdir -p .agents/skills
```

3. **Copy `reproducibility-skill/`** into `.agents/skills/`:

```{.plaintext}
your-project/
└── .agents/
    └── skills/
        └── reproducibility-skill/
            └── SKILL.md
```

Then open the chat panel and use the same prompt:
> *"Prepare a reproducibility package for this project."*

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
The agent picks up **any** skill placed in `.agents/skills/` automatically; exactly what we just did together.
:::

::: {.notes}
This mirrors what we did in the setup slide, so it should feel familiar. Emphasize it's a one-time thing per project, and the `.agents/skills/` convention is all the agent needs.
:::

## What to watch for

We'll stop and read at each gate before moving forward:

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**During the audit**

- Does the agent catch all 10 flags?
- How does it handle `final_merged_v2.csv` — does it ask before guessing?
- What does it say about the meeting notes and `old/` folder?
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**During outline and build**

- The gap table — one concrete action per flag
- The proposed folder restructure (code at root → `code/`)
- The main wrapper script for 3 languages
- Run-check protocol for Stata
:::

::::

→ Switching to VS Code now. Follow along or run it yourself — both are fine.

# Part 4 · Wrap-up {background-color="#002A4F"}

## When is a package "done"?

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="65%"}

1. **Audit clean** — checklist complete, no open flags
2. **DAS complete** — every external input has confirmed source, URL, and access date
3. **One-click entry point** — one path to change per language, packages install, seeds set
4. **Exhibit mapping** — every table and figure maps to a script and an output file
5. **Clean rerun** — ran from scratch, every exhibit regenerated with a fresh timestamp

:::
